Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Enter a username of 4 characters | 3. Fill other required fields | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for username being too short; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Create system user with username exceeding maximum length
Testcase Objective: Verify username must not exceed 40 characters (USERNAME_MAX_LENGTH).
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Enter a username of 41 characters | 3. Fill other required fields | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for username exceeding max length; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Create system user with duplicate username
Testcase Objective: Verify username must be unique across active users (ignoring deleted users).
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Enter a username that already exists | 3. Fill other required fields | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error indicates the username already exists; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Create system user with weak password
Testcase Objective: Verify password must satisfy password strength policy (zxcvbn-based strength check).
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Fill required fields | 3. Enter a weak password (e.g. '1234') | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating the password does not meet strength requirements; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Create system user with password exceeding 64 characters
Testcase Objective: Verify password is rejected when it exceeds the max length of 64 characters.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Fill required fields | 3. Enter a password of 65 characters | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for exceeding max length; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Create system user without selecting an employee
Testcase Objective: Verify empNumber (linked employee) is required and must be an employee accessible to the current user.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Leave the Employee Name field blank | 3. Fill other required fields | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating an employee must be selected; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Create system user without selecting a user role
Testcase Objective: Verify userRoleId is a required field.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users > Add | 2. Leave User Role blank | 3. Fill other required fields | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating user role is required; record is not created.

Testcase Name: Update system user without changing password
Testcase Objective: Verify password field is not required on update when changePassword flag is false.
Steps: 1. Open an existing system user | 2. Do not enable 'change password' option | 3. Update username or role | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: User is updated successfully without requiring a new password.

Testcase Name: Update system user and change password
Testcase Objective: Verify password is required and validated for strength when changePassword flag is true.
Steps: 1. Open an existing system user | 2. Enable 'change password' option | 3. Enter a new strong password | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: User's password is updated successfully.

Testcase Name: Filter users list by username, role, employee and status
Testcase Objective: Verify Users list can be filtered by username, userRoleId, empNumber and status.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users | 2. Apply username/role/employee/status filters | 3. Click Search
Expected Result: Only users matching all applied filters are displayed.

Testcase Name: Attempt to delete the currently logged-in user's own account
Testcase Objective: Verify a user cannot delete their own logged-in account (undeletable id business rule).
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users | 2. Select the currently logged-in user's own account | 3. Click Delete
Expected Result: Deletion is blocked with a validation error; the current user's account is not deleted.

Testcase Name: Delete one or more system users (not self)
Testcase Objective: Verify selected system users (other than the current logged-in user) can be bulk deleted.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > User Management > Users | 2. Select one or more other users | 3. Click Delete | 4. Confirm
Expected Result: Selected users are deleted and no longer appear in the list.

Testcase Objective: Verify username validation endpoint returns valid=true for a username not already in use.
Steps: 1. On Add User screen, type a username that does not exist | 2. Trigger username availability check
Expected Result: Response indicates the username is valid/available for use.

Testcase Objective: Verify username validation endpoint returns valid=false for a username already in use.
Steps: 1. On Add User screen, type a username that already exists | 2. Trigger username availability check
Expected Result: Response indicates the username is not valid/available (already taken).

Testcase Name: Validate username while editing own user (excluding self)
Testcase Objective: Verify passing userId excludes that user's own current username from the uniqueness check.
Steps: 1. Open Edit User screen for an existing user | 2. Keep username unchanged and trigger validation, passing userId
Expected Result: Response indicates the username is valid since the user's own record is excluded from the check.

Testcase Objective: Verify username validation rejects values exceeding max length of 40 characters.
Steps: 1. Type a username of 41 characters | 2. Trigger username availability check
Expected Result: Validation error is returned for exceeding max length.

Testcase Objective: Verify current email/SMTP configuration can be viewed, defaulting to SMTP/Login/SSL when not yet configured.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration
Expected Result: Existing email configuration is displayed, or sensible defaults are shown if unconfigured.

Testcase Name: Configure email with Sendmail mail type
Testcase Objective: Verify mailType can be set to sendmail without requiring SMTP host/username/password.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration | 2. Select Mail Type = Sendmail | 3. Enter a valid Send As email address | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Configuration is saved successfully without requiring SMTP-specific fields.

Testcase Name: Configure email with SMTP mail type and Login auth
Testcase Objective: Verify smtpHost and smtpAuthType become required when mailType is smtp/secure_smtp, and smtpUsername/smtpPassword become required when authType is login.

Expected Result: Configuration is saved successfully with all SMTP fields persisted.

Testcase Name: Configure SMTP mail type without SMTP host
Testcase Objective: Verify smtpHost is required when mailType is smtp or secure_smtp.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration | 2. Select Mail Type = SMTP | 3. Leave SMTP Host blank | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating SMTP host is required; configuration is not saved.

Testcase Name: Configure email with invalid Send As email format
Testcase Objective: Verify sentAs field must be a valid email address (max 100 chars).
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration | 2. Enter an invalid value in Send As field (e.g. 'notanemail') | 3. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for invalid email format; configuration is not saved.

Testcase Name: Configure email with unsupported mail type
Testcase Objective: Verify mailType must be one of sendmail, smtp, or secure_smtp.
Steps: 1. Send update request with mailType set to an unsupported value | 2. Submit
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating mailType is not an allowed value; configuration is not saved.

Testcase Name: Configure email with unsupported SMTP auth type
Testcase Objective: Verify smtpAuthType must be one of the allowed auth type values (login/none).
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration | 2. Select Mail Type = SMTP | 3. Submit an unsupported Auth Type value | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating the auth type is not allowed; configuration is not saved.

Testcase Name: Send a test email after saving valid configuration
Testcase Objective: Verify providing a testEmailAddress triggers a test email send and reports success/failure status.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration | 2. Fill valid SMTP configuration | 3. Enter a valid Test Email Address | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Configuration is saved and testEmailStatus in the response indicates whether the test email was sent successfully (1) or failed (0).

Testcase Name: Send a test email with invalid test email address format
Testcase Objective: Verify testEmailAddress must be a valid email format (max 250 chars) when provided.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Mail Configuration | 2. Enter an invalid value in Test Email Address field | 3. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for invalid email format; configuration is not saved.

Testcase Objective: Verify all available email subscription types (leave application, assignment, approval, cancellation, rejection) are listed.

Testcase Objective: Verify updating a subscription id that does not exist returns a not-found error.

Testcase Name: Add a subscriber to a valid email subscription

Expected Result: Subscriber is added successfully to the selected email subscription.

Testcase Name: Add subscriber with missing name or email

Expected Result: Validation error is shown for the missing required field(s); subscriber is not added.

Testcase Name: Add subscriber with invalid email format
Testcase Objective: Verify subscriber email must be a valid email format (max 100 chars).
Steps: 1. Open a subscription's subscriber list | 2. Click Add | 3. Enter an invalid email address | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for invalid email format; subscriber is not added.

Testcase Name: Add subscriber with duplicate email within the same subscription
Testcase Objective: Verify subscriber email must be unique within the same email subscription (matchValues on emailNotification).
Steps: 1. Open a subscription's subscriber list | 2. Add a subscriber with an email already subscribed to this subscription | 3. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error indicates the email already exists for this subscription; subscriber is not added.

Testcase Name: Add subscriber to an invalid subscription id
Testcase Objective: Verify emailSubscriptionId must be one of the allowed subscription types.
Steps: 1. Send create request with an emailSubscriptionId that is not a valid subscription type
Expected Result: Validation error is shown indicating the subscription id is not allowed.

Testcase Name: List subscribers for a subscription with pagination
Testcase Objective: Verify subscribers for a given subscription can be listed with sorting and pagination.
Steps: 1. Open a subscription's subscriber list | 2. Apply sorting and page through results
Expected Result: Subscribers are listed correctly sorted and paginated with correct total count and subscription name in meta.

Testcase Objective: Verify an existing subscriber's name and email can be updated.
Steps: 1. Open a subscription's subscriber list | 2. Edit an existing subscriber's name or email | 3. Click Save
Expected Result: Subscriber details are updated successfully.

Testcase Name: Delete one or more subscribers from a subscription
Testcase Objective: Verify selected subscribers can be bulk deleted from a subscription.
Steps: 1. Open a subscription's subscriber list | 2. Select one or more subscribers | 3. Click Delete | 4. Confirm
Expected Result: Selected subscribers are removed from the subscription list.

Testcase Objective: Verify translation strings for a specific languageId can be listed.

Testcase Objective: Verify translations list can be filtered by a valid I18N group id.

Testcase Name: List translations for a non-existent language id

Testcase Objective: Verify all translation groups (module groupings for language strings) can be listed.

Testcase Name: List I18N groups with sorting and pagination
Testcase Objective: Verify the group list supports sortField, sortOrder, limit and offset.

Testcase Name: View current default localization language and date format
Testcase Objective: Verify the admin panel's default display language and date format can be retrieved.

Testcase Name: Update default language to a supported language

Testcase Name: Update default date format to a supported format
Testcase Objective: Verify default date format can be updated to any value from the supported date formats list.

Expected Result: Default date format is updated successfully.

Testcase Name: Update default date format to an unsupported value

Testcase Name: List all configurable modules with status

Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Modules | 2. Attempt to toggle PIM module to disabled | 3. Click Save

Testcase Objective: Verify non-core modules such as Leave can be toggled on and off.

Testcase Objective: Verify Mobile module toggle updates the mobile OAuth client status accordingly.

Testcase Name: Update modules with an invalid boolean value

Testcase Name: Create a subunit with unit id and description

Testcase Name: Create a subunit with missing name

Testcase Name: View organization structure in tree mode

Testcase Name: Attempt to delete the top-level organization unit (id=1)

Testcase Name: Add a currency to a pay grade with valid min/max salary
Testcase Objective: Verify a currency can be added to a pay grade with minSalary less than maxSalary, both within allowed range and decimal precision.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Job > Pay Grades > select a Pay Grade > Add Currency | 2. Select a currency | 3. Enter min salary and max salary (min < max) | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Currency with min/max salary range is added successfully to the pay grade.

Testcase Name: Add a currency with min salary greater than or equal to max salary
Testcase Objective: Verify the business rule that minSalary must be less than maxSalary (unless minSalary is 0).
Steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen | 2. Select a currency | 3. Enter min salary equal to or greater than max salary | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Error is returned: 'Min salary should be less than max salary'; currency is not added.

Testcase Name: Add a currency with min salary of 0
Testcase Objective: Verify minSalary of exactly 0 is treated as a special case and does not trigger the min<max comparison bypass incorrectly.
Steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen | 2. Select a currency | 3. Set min salary = 0 and max salary = any positive value | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Currency is added successfully with min salary 0.

Testcase Name: Add a currency with salary exceeding maximum allowed value
Testcase Objective: Verify salary values must be less than 1,000,000,000 (PARAM_RULE_SALARY_MAX_VALUE).
Steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen | 2. Select a currency | 3. Enter max salary >= 1,000,000,000 | 4. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for exceeding the maximum allowed salary value; currency is not added.

Testcase Name: Add a currency with more than 2 decimal places in salary
Testcase Objective: Verify salary values only allow up to 2 decimal places (DECIMAL rule 0/1/2).
Steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen | 2. Enter a salary value with 3 decimal places (e.g. 1000.123) | 3. Click Save
Expected Result: Validation error is shown for invalid decimal precision; currency is not added.

Testcase Name: Add a currency to a non-existent pay grade
Testcase Objective: Verify adding a currency fails if the specified payGradeId does not exist.
Steps: 1. Send create request with a payGradeId that does not exist
Expected Result: A 404 Record Not Found response is returned; currency is not added.

Testcase Name: Update min/max salary for an existing pay grade currency
Testcase Objective: Verify min and max salary for an already-assigned currency can be updated.
Steps: 1. Open an existing pay grade's currency list | 2. Edit an assigned currency's min/max salary | 3. Click Save
Expected Result: Min/max salary values are updated successfully for that currency.

Testcase Name: Delete one or more currencies from a pay grade
Testcase Objective: Verify selected currencies can be bulk removed from a pay grade.
Steps: 1. Open a pay grade's currency list | 2. Select one or more currencies | 3. Click Delete | 4. Confirm
Expected Result: Selected currencies are removed from the pay grade's currency list.

Testcase Name: List currencies available to assign to a pay grade
Testcase Objective: Verify only currencies not already assigned to a given pay grade are listed as allowed/available.
Steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen | 2. Open the currency selection dropdown
Expected Result: Only currencies not yet assigned to the pay grade are listed as selectable options.

Testcase Name: List allowed currencies with sorting and pagination
Testcase Objective: Verify the allowed currencies list supports sortField, sortOrder, limit and offset.
Steps: 1. Request allowed currencies for a pay grade with sort and pagination parameters
Expected Result: Allowed currencies are returned correctly sorted and paginated with correct total count.

Testcase Name: List allowed currencies for a non-existent pay grade
Testcase Objective: Verify requesting allowed currencies for an invalid payGradeId is handled correctly.
Steps: 1. Send GET request for allowed currencies with a payGradeId that does not exist
Expected Result: Validation error or empty result set is returned with no server error.

Testcase Name: Retrieve job specification attachment for a job title that has one
Testcase Objective: Verify the job specification file metadata/content can be retrieved for a job title with an attached specification.
Steps: 1. Navigate to Admin > Job Titles | 2. Open a job title that has an attached specification | 3. Download/view the specification

Testcase Name: Retrieve job specification for a job title with no attachment
Testcase Objective: Verify requesting the job specification for a job title without one returns a not-found error.

Testcase Name: Retrieve job specification for a non-existent job title id
Testcase Objective: Verify requesting a job specification using an invalid jobTitleId is handled correctly.

Testcase Name: Punch in successfully with valid date, time and timezone
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee can punch in successfully with all valid required fields.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Navigate to Time > Attendance > Punch In/Out | 3. Confirm current date, time, timezoneOffset and timezoneName are populated | 4. Click Punch In
Expected Result: Attendance record is created with state 'PUNCHED IN' and punch-in date/time/timezone are saved correctly.

Testcase Name: Punch in fails when date field is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'date' field is not provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send Punch In request without 'date' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a validation error indicating 'date' is required; no attendance record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in fails when time field is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'time' field is not provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send Punch In request without 'time' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a validation error indicating 'time' is required; no attendance record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in fails when timezoneOffset is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'timezoneOffset' field is not provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send Punch In request without 'timezoneOffset' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a validation error for missing timezoneOffset; no attendance record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in fails when timezoneName is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'timezoneName' field is not provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send Punch In request without 'timezoneName' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a validation error for missing timezoneName; no attendance record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in fails with invalid time format
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in rejects a time value that does not match the required 'H:i' format.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send Punch In request with time='25:99' (invalid format)
Expected Result: API returns a TIME format validation error and no attendance record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in note accepted up to 250 characters
Testcase Objective: Verify the punch-in note field is accepted when it is at the maximum allowed length of 250 characters.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Enter a punch-in note of exactly 250 characters | 3. Click Punch In
Expected Result: Punch in succeeds and the 250-character note is saved without truncation.

Testcase Name: Punch in fails when note exceeds 250 characters
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in is rejected when the note field exceeds the 250 character maximum length.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Enter a punch-in note of 251 characters | 3. Click Punch In
Expected Result: API returns a LENGTH validation error for punchInNote/note and no attendance record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in blocked when an overlapping punched-in record already exists
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in is rejected with 'Punch-In Overlap Found' when the employee already has an overlapping open attendance record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who already has an active punched-in record | 2. Attempt to Punch In again with a date/time that overlaps the existing open record
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Punch-In Overlap Found'; no new record is created.

Testcase Name: Punch in rejected when system time is altered beyond tolerance and 'Allow employees to change time' is disabled
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in fails with 'Provided Date And Time Invalid' when the configuration disallows changing current time and the supplied date/time differs from the actual server time by more than 180 seconds.
Steps: 1. As Admin, disable 'Allow Employees to Change Punch In/Out Time' in Attendance Configuration | 2. Login as ESS user | 3. Submit Punch In with a date/time more than 3 minutes different from the real current time
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Provided Date And Time Invalid'; punch in is rejected.

Testcase Name: Punch in succeeds when time is within +/-180 second tolerance and time-change is disabled
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in succeeds when 'Allow employees to change time' is disabled but the supplied date/time is within the 180-second margin of the actual current time.
Steps: 1. As Admin, disable 'Allow Employees to Change Punch In/Out Time' | 2. Login as ESS user | 3. Submit Punch In using the real current date/time (within 3 minutes)
Expected Result: Punch in succeeds and attendance record is created with state 'PUNCHED IN'.

Testcase Name: Punch in succeeds without an optional note
Testcase Objective: Verify punch in succeeds when the optional 'note' field is left blank.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Leave the punch-in note field empty | 3. Click Punch In
Expected Result: Punch in succeeds and the attendance record is saved with a null/empty note.

Testcase Name: Punch out successfully after an active punch in
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee who is currently punched in can punch out successfully.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is currently punched in | 2. Navigate to Time > Attendance > Punch In/Out | 3. Click Punch Out with valid date/time/timezone
Expected Result: The open attendance record is updated to state 'PUNCHED OUT' with punch-out date/time/timezone saved.

Testcase Name: Punch out fails when employee has no active punch-in record
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out is rejected with 'Cannot Proceed Punch Out Employee Already Punched Out' when there is no open punch-in record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is already punched out (no open record) | 2. Attempt to Punch Out
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Cannot Proceed Punch Out Employee Already Punched Out'.

Testcase Name: Punch out fails when date field is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out request is rejected when the required 'date' field is not provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Send Punch Out request without 'date' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a validation error indicating 'date' is required; record remains in PUNCHED IN state.

Testcase Name: Punch out fails when time field is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out request is rejected when the required 'time' field is not provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Send Punch Out request without 'time' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a validation error indicating 'time' is required; record remains in PUNCHED IN state.

Testcase Name: Punch out fails with invalid timezoneOffset value
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out is rejected when timezoneOffset does not match the expected TIMEZONE_OFFSET format.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Send Punch Out request with timezoneOffset='ABC'
Expected Result: API returns a TIMEZONE_OFFSET validation error; punch out is rejected.

Testcase Name: Punch out blocked when new punch-out time overlaps another attendance record
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out is rejected with 'Punch-Out Overlap Found' when the resulting punched interval overlaps an existing attendance record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Enter a punch-out date/time that overlaps another existing attendance record | 3. Click Punch Out
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Punch-Out Overlap Found'; record is not updated.

Testcase Name: Punch out succeeds with an optional note within limit
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out succeeds when an optional note of valid length is provided.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Enter a punch-out note of 50 characters | 3. Click Punch Out
Expected Result: Punch out succeeds and the note is saved with the attendance record.

Testcase Name: Punch out rejected when system time is altered beyond tolerance and time-change is disabled
Testcase Objective: Verify punch out fails with 'Provided Date And Time Invalid' when 'Allow employees to change time' is disabled and supplied time differs from actual time by more than 180 seconds.
Steps: 1. As Admin, disable 'Allow Employees to Change Punch In/Out Time' | 2. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 3. Submit Punch Out with a date/time more than 3 minutes off from real current time
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Provided Date And Time Invalid'; punch out is rejected.

Testcase Name: Edit punch-in time of an active (currently punched-in) record
Testcase Objective: Verify a user with edit permission can successfully update the punch-in date/time of a record that is still in PUNCHED IN state.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with an active punched-in record | 2. Navigate to the attendance record and edit the punch-in time | 3. Save changes via PUT /attendance/records/{id}
Expected Result: Record is updated with the new punch-in date/time/note; no overlap detected.

Testcase Name: Edit both punch-in and punch-out time of a completed record
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can update both punch-in and punch-out date/time of a fully punched-out attendance record.
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission on a completed attendance record | 2. Edit punch-in date/time and punch-out date/time | 3. Save changes
Expected Result: Record is updated successfully with both new punch-in and punch-out timestamps.

Testcase Name: Edit fails when only timezoneOffset is supplied without timezoneName
Testcase Objective: Verify editing a record fails with 'Valid Timezone Offset and Timezone Name Must Be Provided' when only one of the timezone fields is supplied.
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission | 2. Submit edit request with punchInOffset set but punchInTimezoneName omitted | 3. Save changes
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Valid Timezone Offset and Timezone Name Must Be Provided'.

Testcase Name: Edit completed record fails when punchOutTime is missing while punchOutDate is provided
Testcase Objective: Verify editing a PUNCHED OUT record fails with 'Punch Out Date And Time Should Not Be Null' when punchOutDate is given but punchOutTime is null.
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission on a completed record | 2. Submit edit request with punchOutDate set and punchOutTime omitted | 3. Save changes
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Punch Out Date And Time Should Not Be Null'.

Testcase Name: Edit blocked when new punch-in time overlaps another record
Testcase Objective: Verify editing the punch-in time is rejected with 'Punch-In Overlap Found' if the new time overlaps an existing attendance record for the same employee.
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission | 2. Edit punch-in time to a value overlapping another existing record | 3. Save changes
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Punch-In Overlap Found'; record is not updated.

Testcase Name: Edit blocked when new punch-out time overlaps another record
Testcase Objective: Verify editing punch-out time of a completed record is rejected with 'Punch-Out Overlap Found' when the new interval overlaps another attendance record.
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission on a completed record | 2. Edit punch-out time to a value overlapping another existing record | 3. Save changes
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Punch-Out Overlap Found'; record is not updated.

Testcase Name: Edit denied for a record the user is not authorized to modify
Testcase Objective: Verify a user without the appropriate edit-punch-time workflow permission for the record's owner receives a 403 Forbidden.
Steps: 1. Login as an ESS user with no supervisory relationship to the record owner | 2. Attempt PUT /attendance/records/{id} for another employee's record
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; record is not modified.

Testcase Name: Edit fails for a non-existent attendance record ID
Testcase Objective: Verify editing an attendance record with an ID that does not exist returns a 404 Record Not Found error.
Steps: 1. Login as an authorized user | 2. Send PUT /attendance/records/{id} using an ID that does not exist in the system
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 404 Record Not Found.

Testcase Name: Delete attendance record via /attendance/records/{id} is not implemented
Testcase Objective: Verify calling DELETE on the single-record attendance endpoint returns a Not Implemented response, confirming deletion must go through the employee-scoped delete endpoint.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Send DELETE /api/v2/attendance/records/{id}
Expected Result: API returns a Not Implemented (405/501) response; no record is deleted.

Testcase Name: Edit fails with invalid punchInDate format
Testcase Objective: Verify editing a record is rejected when punchInDate does not conform to the expected API date format.
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission | 2. Submit edit request with punchInDate='13/40/2026' (invalid format) | 3. Save changes
Expected Result: API returns an API_DATE validation error; record is not updated.

Testcase Name: Edit record ID parameter must be a positive integer
Testcase Objective: Verify editing an attendance record fails validation when the {id} path parameter is not a positive integer (e.g. 0 or negative).
Steps: 1. Login as user with edit permission | 2. Send PUT /attendance/records/-1
Expected Result: API returns a POSITIVE rule validation error; request is rejected before any DB lookup.

Testcase Name: Delete a single own attendance record successfully
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee with delete permission can delete one of their own attendance records.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Navigate to My Attendance Records | 3. Select one record and click Delete | 4. Confirm deletion
Expected Result: The selected record is removed and returned in the response's list of deleted IDs.

Testcase Name: Delete multiple own attendance records in a single request
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee can delete several of their own attendance records in one DELETE request using an array of IDs.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Select multiple attendance records | 3. Click Delete and confirm
Expected Result: All selected records are deleted successfully and returned in the response.

Testcase Name: Delete fails when ids array is empty
Testcase Objective: Verify deletion is rejected with 'No IDs Found' when an empty ids array is submitted.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send DELETE request to /attendance/employees/{empNumber}/records with ids=[]
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'No IDs Found'; nothing is deleted.

Testcase Name: Delete fails when attempting to delete a record not owned by the requesting employee
Testcase Objective: Verify deletion is denied with 403 Forbidden when one or more supplied record IDs do not belong to the target employee.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user A | 2. Send DELETE request including an attendance record ID that belongs to employee B
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; no records are deleted.

Testcase Name: Delete own record denied when 'Employee can edit/delete own attendance' is disabled
Testcase Objective: Verify an ESS user cannot delete their own attendance record when the corresponding attendance configuration is turned off.
Steps: 1. As Admin, disable 'Employee can edit/delete own attendance records' in Attendance Configuration | 2. Login as ESS user | 3. Attempt to delete an own attendance record
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; the record remains in the system.

Testcase Name: Delete fails when ids parameter is not an array
Testcase Objective: Verify the delete request is rejected by validation when the 'ids' parameter is not of array type.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Send DELETE request with ids='5' (string instead of array)
Expected Result: API returns an ARRAY_TYPE validation error; request is rejected.

Testcase Name: List own attendance records defaults to today's date when no filters supplied
Testcase Objective: Verify that when no date, fromDate or toDate is supplied, the record list defaults to showing only today's attendance records.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Navigate to My Attendance Records without applying any filter
Expected Result: Only attendance records for the current date are displayed along with total count and total worked-hours summary.

Testcase Name: List own attendance records filtered by a specific date
Testcase Objective: Verify filtering attendance records by the 'date' query parameter returns only records for that date.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Apply date filter for a specific past date | 3. View results
Expected Result: Only records matching the specified date are returned.

Testcase Name: List own attendance records using a fromDate/toDate range
Testcase Objective: Verify filtering by fromDate and toDate returns all attendance records within that inclusive date range.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Set fromDate and toDate spanning a week | 3. View results
Expected Result: All attendance records between fromDate 00:00:00 and toDate 23:59:59 are returned.

Testcase Name: List fails when fromDate is later than toDate
Testcase Objective: Verify the API rejects the request with an invalid parameter error when fromDate is chronologically after toDate.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Set fromDate=2026-08-10 and toDate=2026-08-01 | 3. Submit the filter
Expected Result: API returns an invalid parameter error referencing fromDate and toDate; no results are returned.

Testcase Name: List own attendance records with pagination
Testcase Objective: Verify limit and offset query parameters correctly paginate the attendance record list.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with more than 10 attendance records | 2. Request the list with limit=5 and offset=5
Expected Result: Exactly 5 records starting from the 6th record are returned, with correct 'total' meta value.

Testcase Name: List own attendance records sorted by punch-in time
Testcase Objective: Verify the sortField and sortOrder parameters correctly order the returned attendance records.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Request the list with sortField=punchInUserTime and sortOrder=DESC
Expected Result: Records are returned in descending order of punch-in time.

Testcase Name: Total worked-hours summary is calculated correctly for the filtered period
Testcase Objective: Verify the 'sum' meta object (hours, minutes, label) accurately reflects the total working time of the returned records.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with multiple completed attendance records for the day | 2. Request the attendance record list for that day
Expected Result: The 'sum' object in meta reflects the correct total hours and minutes worked, matching the sum of individual record durations.

Testcase Name: Admin adds a punch-in record on behalf of a subordinate employee
Testcase Objective: Verify an Admin user can create (proxy punch in) an attendance record for any employee via /attendance/employees/{empNumber}/records.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Navigate to Employee Attendance and select an employee | 3. Enter punch-in date/time/timezone and save
Expected Result: A new attendance record is created for the selected employee with state 'PUNCHED IN'.

Testcase Name: Supervisor adds a punch-in record for a direct subordinate
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor with proxy punch-in permission can add an attendance record for their direct report.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Select a direct subordinate employee | 3. Enter punch-in details and save
Expected Result: Attendance record is created for the subordinate employee.

Testcase Name: Supervisor is blocked from adding a punch-in record for an employee outside their reporting hierarchy
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor cannot create an attendance record for an employee who is not their subordinate.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Attempt to POST an attendance record using the empNumber of a non-subordinate employee
Expected Result: API returns a validation/forbidden error (IN_ACCESSIBLE_EMP_NUMBERS); no record is created.

Testcase Name: Supervisor punches out (proxy) a subordinate who is currently punched in
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor can complete (punch out) an open attendance record for a subordinate employee.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Select a subordinate with an active punch-in record | 3. Enter punch-out date/time and save
Expected Result: The subordinate's record is updated to state 'PUNCHED OUT' with correct punch-out details.

Testcase Name: Admin deletes an attendance record belonging to any employee
Testcase Objective: Verify an Admin can delete attendance record(s) belonging to any employee in the system.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Navigate to an employee's attendance records | 3. Select a record and delete it
Expected Result: The record is deleted successfully regardless of which employee owns it.

Testcase Name: Supervisor delete of subordinate's record blocked when 'Supervisor can modify attendance' is disabled
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor cannot delete a subordinate's attendance record when the corresponding configuration toggle is turned off.
Steps: 1. As Admin, disable 'Supervisor can add/edit/delete subordinate attendance records' | 2. Login as Supervisor | 3. Attempt to delete a subordinate's attendance record
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; the record is not deleted.

Testcase Name: Supervisor lists attendance records for a specific subordinate via empNumber
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor can retrieve the attendance record list of a subordinate by specifying the empNumber query parameter.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Request GET /attendance/employees/{empNumber}/records for a subordinate
Expected Result: Attendance records for the specified subordinate are returned along with total count and worked-time summary.

Testcase Name: List employee attendance records fails when empNumber is not provided
Testcase Objective: Verify the employee-scoped attendance record list requires the empNumber path parameter and rejects requests without it.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Send GET /attendance/employees/records without a valid empNumber
Expected Result: API returns a required-field validation error for empNumber.

Testcase Name: List employee attendance records fails for a non-existent employee number
Testcase Objective: Verify the API rejects the request when empNumber does not correspond to an existing employee (ENTITY_ID_EXISTS rule).
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Send GET /attendance/employees/999999/records using a non-existent empNumber
Expected Result: API returns an ENTITY_ID_EXISTS validation error; no records are returned.

Testcase Name: ESS user is forbidden from viewing another employee's attendance records directly
Testcase Objective: Verify an ESS-role user without supervisory relationship cannot view another employee's attendance records, per EmployeeDataGroupReadPermissionRule.
Steps: 1. Login as an ESS user with no subordinates | 2. Attempt GET /attendance/employees/{otherEmpNumber}/records for an unrelated employee
Expected Result: API returns a Forbidden error; attendance records are not disclosed.

Testcase Name: Get attendance summary for all accessible employees for the current day
Testcase Objective: Verify the summary report defaults to today's date and lists summary rows for all employees accessible to the logged-in user when no empNumber is specified.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin or Supervisor | 2. Navigate to Attendance Summary report without filters
Expected Result: Summary rows are returned for all accessible employees for the current date, with a correct total count.

Testcase Name: Get attendance summary filtered by a specific employee
Testcase Objective: Verify supplying the empNumber query parameter restricts the summary report to that single employee.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Apply empNumber filter for one subordinate | 3. View the summary report
Expected Result: Only the summary row for the specified employee is returned.

Testcase Name: Get attendance summary using a fromDate/toDate range
Testcase Objective: Verify the summary report correctly aggregates data across a custom date range.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Set fromDate and toDate spanning one month | 3. View the summary report
Expected Result: Summary rows reflect aggregated attendance data for the full date range specified.

Testcase Name: Attendance summary fails when fromDate is after toDate
Testcase Objective: Verify the summary report rejects an invalid date range where fromDate is later than toDate.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Set fromDate=2026-09-30 and toDate=2026-09-01 | 3. Submit the filter
Expected Result: API returns an invalid parameter error for fromDate/toDate; no summary is returned.

Testcase Name: Attendance summary blocked for an employee outside the supervisor's scope
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor cannot retrieve the attendance summary of an employee who is not their subordinate.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Request summary with empNumber of a non-subordinate employee
Expected Result: API returns a Forbidden/validation error (IN_ACCESSIBLE_ENTITY_ID); summary is not returned.

Testcase Name: Attendance summary supports sorting and pagination
Testcase Objective: Verify sortField, sortOrder, limit and offset parameters work correctly on the summary endpoint.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin with more than 10 employees | 2. Request summary with limit=5, offset=0, sortField=employeeName
Expected Result: Exactly 5 summary rows are returned, sorted by employee name.

Testcase Name: Attendance summary fails for a non-existent employee number
Testcase Objective: Verify the summary endpoint validates that the supplied empNumber corresponds to an existing employee.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Request summary with empNumber=999999 (does not exist)
Expected Result: API returns an ENTITY_ID_EXISTS validation error.

Testcase Name: ESS user's attendance summary is scoped to only their own record
Testcase Objective: Verify that when an ESS user (with no subordinates) requests the summary without empNumber, only their own accessible record is included.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with no subordinates | 2. Request the attendance summary without any empNumber filter
Expected Result: Only the logged-in user's own summary row is returned, based on their accessible employee IDs.

Testcase Objective: Verify Admin can fetch the current values of all three attendance configuration toggles.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Navigate to Admin > Configuration > Attendance
Expected Result: The response returns canUserChangeCurrentTime, canUserModifyAttendance and canSupervisorModifyAttendance with their current boolean values.

Testcase Name: Admin enables 'Allow Employees to Change Punch In/Out Time'
Testcase Objective: Verify enabling canUserChangeCurrentTime is persisted and reflected in subsequent punch actions.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Set canUserChangeCurrentTime=true | 3. Save configuration
Expected Result: Configuration is updated successfully; employees can now submit punch times different from the real current time.

Testcase Name: Admin disables 'Employee can edit/delete own attendance records'
Testcase Objective: Verify disabling canUserModifyAttendance prevents ESS users from editing/deleting their own attendance going forward.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Set canUserModifyAttendance=false | 3. Save configuration
Expected Result: Configuration is updated; subsequent edit/delete attempts by ESS users on their own records are forbidden.

Testcase Name: Admin enables 'Supervisor can add/edit/delete subordinate attendance records'
Testcase Objective: Verify enabling canSupervisorModifyAttendance allows supervisors to manage subordinate attendance records.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Set canSupervisorModifyAttendance=true | 3. Save configuration
Expected Result: Configuration is updated; supervisors can now add/edit/delete records for their subordinates.

Testcase Name: Update configuration fails when a required boolean field is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify the update request is rejected when one of the three required configuration fields is omitted.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Send PUT /attendance/configs without canSupervisorModifyAttendance
Expected Result: API returns a required-field validation error; configuration is not changed.

Testcase Name: Update configuration fails with a non-boolean value
Testcase Objective: Verify the update request is rejected when a configuration field is supplied as a non-boolean type (e.g., string 'yes').
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Send PUT /attendance/configs with canUserChangeCurrentTime='yes'
Expected Result: API returns a BOOL_TYPE validation error; configuration is not changed.

Testcase Name: Non-admin user is forbidden from accessing attendance configuration
Testcase Objective: Verify a user without Admin privileges cannot view or update the attendance configuration.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS/Supervisor user | 2. Attempt to access Admin > Configuration > Attendance
Expected Result: Access is denied (403 Forbidden or menu item not visible).

Testcase Name: Configuration changes persist after being saved
Testcase Objective: Verify that after updating the configuration, re-fetching it returns the newly saved values.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Update all three configuration toggles to new values and save | 3. Refresh/re-fetch GET /attendance/configs
Expected Result: The GET response reflects the exact values that were saved in the previous update.

Testcase Name: Check punch-in overlap for a free (non-overlapping) time slot returns valid=true
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/punch-in/overlaps returns valid=true for a date/time that does not overlap any existing record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with no attendance record at the checked time | 2. Call GET /attendance/punch-in/overlaps with date, time, timezoneOffset
Expected Result: Response returns {valid: true}, indicating no punch-in overlap.

Testcase Name: Check punch-in overlap for a time slot within an existing open record returns valid=false
Testcase Objective: Verify the punch-in overlap check correctly detects an overlap with an existing punched-in record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with an active punched-in record | 2. Call GET /attendance/punch-in/overlaps using a time that falls inside the existing record's interval
Expected Result: Response returns {valid: false}, indicating a punch-in overlap was found.

Testcase Name: Punch-in overlap check fails when required 'date' parameter is missing
Testcase Objective: Verify the punch-in overlap check endpoint enforces the required date parameter.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call GET /attendance/punch-in/overlaps without the 'date' parameter
Expected Result: API returns a required-field validation error for 'date'.

Testcase Name: Check punch-out overlap for a free time slot returns valid=true
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/punch-out/overlaps returns valid=true when the proposed punch-out time does not overlap any other record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Call GET /attendance/punch-out/overlaps with a non-conflicting date/time
Expected Result: Response returns {valid: true}.

Testcase Name: Check punch-out overlap for a conflicting time slot returns valid=false
Testcase Objective: Verify the punch-out overlap check correctly detects a conflict with another existing attendance record.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who is punched in | 2. Call GET /attendance/punch-out/overlaps using a time that overlaps another existing record
Expected Result: Response returns {valid: false}.

Testcase Name: Edit punch-in overlap check returns 404 for a non-existent recordId
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/records/punch-in-overlaps returns Record Not Found when recordId does not exist.
Steps: 1. Login as authorized user | 2. Call GET /attendance/records/punch-in-overlaps with recordId=999999
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 404 Record Not Found.

Testcase Name: Edit punch-in overlap check denied for a record the user cannot access
Testcase Objective: Verify a user without visibility into another employee's attendance record is forbidden from checking its punch-in overlap.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with no relation to the record owner | 2. Call GET /attendance/records/punch-in-overlaps with recordId belonging to an unrelated employee
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 403 Forbidden.

Testcase Name: Edit punch-out overlap check requires both punchOutDate and punchOutTime
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/records/punch-out-overlaps enforces punchOutDate and punchOutTime as required parameters (unlike the punch-in overlap edit check where they are optional).
Steps: 1. Login as authorized user | 2. Call GET /attendance/records/punch-out-overlaps with a valid recordId but omit punchOutDate
Expected Result: API returns a required-field validation error for punchOutDate.

Testcase Name: Supervisor checks punch-in overlap for a subordinate using empNumber
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor can check punch-in overlap on behalf of a subordinate by supplying the empNumber query parameter.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Call GET /attendance/punch-in/overlaps with empNumber of a subordinate and a valid date/time
Expected Result: Response correctly returns the overlap validity for the specified subordinate's attendance records.

Testcase Name: List all available timezones with their current UTC offsets
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/timezones returns the full list of system timezones with name, label and offset.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Navigate to Punch In/Out and open the Timezone dropdown
Expected Result: All available timezones are listed, each with a name, +/-HH:mm label and numeric offset.

Testcase Name: Filter timezones by partial name match
Testcase Objective: Verify supplying the timezoneName query parameter filters the timezone list to matching entries only.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Call GET /attendance/timezones?timezoneName=America
Expected Result: Only timezone identifiers containing 'America' (case-insensitive) are returned.

Testcase Name: Filter timezones with a name that matches no entries returns an empty list
Testcase Objective: Verify searching for a non-matching timezone name returns an empty result set instead of an error.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Call GET /attendance/timezones?timezoneName=Xyzabc123
Expected Result: Response returns an empty data array and total=0, with HTTP 200.

Testcase Name: Timezone list is sorted by UTC offset
Testcase Objective: Verify the returned timezone list is ordered from the lowest to the highest UTC offset for usability in the dropdown.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Retrieve the full timezone list | 3. Inspect the order of the 'offset' values
Expected Result: Timezones appear in ascending order of offset value.

Testcase Name: Get current server date and time in UTC
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/current-datetime returns the server's current date and time normalized to UTC.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Open Punch In/Out page which loads the current date/time | 3. Call GET /attendance/current-datetime
Expected Result: Response returns the current date and time in UTC, matching the server clock within a few seconds.

Testcase Name: Current date/time response format is valid
Testcase Objective: Verify the DateTimeModel response contains correctly structured date/time fields consumable by the client.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Call GET /attendance/current-datetime | 3. Inspect the response payload structure
Expected Result: Response 'data' object contains a well-formed date/time value with no null or malformed fields.

Testcase Name: Current date/time endpoint ignores an 'id' path parameter
Testcase Objective: Verify the endpoint excludes the standard 'id' parameter from validation since it is a singleton resource with no identifier.
Steps: 1. Login as any user | 2. Call GET /attendance/current-datetime (no id required)
Expected Result: Request succeeds without requiring or validating an 'id' parameter.

Testcase Name: Get the latest attendance record for the logged-in user
Testcase Objective: Verify GET /attendance/records/latest returns the most recent attendance record for the authenticated user when no empNumber is supplied.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with at least one attendance record | 2. Call GET /attendance/records/latest without empNumber
Expected Result: The most recent attendance record belonging to the logged-in user is returned.

Testcase Name: Get the latest attendance record for another employee via empNumber
Testcase Objective: Verify a Supervisor/Admin can retrieve the latest attendance record of a specific employee by supplying empNumber, subject to accessible-employee validation.
Steps: 1. Login as Supervisor | 2. Call GET /attendance/records/latest?empNumber={subordinateEmpNumber}
Expected Result: The latest attendance record for the specified subordinate is returned.

Testcase Name: Latest attendance record returns 404 when the employee has no records
Testcase Objective: Verify the endpoint returns a Record Not Found error when the target employee has no attendance records at all.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user with zero attendance records | 2. Call GET /attendance/records/latest
Expected Result: API returns HTTP 404 Record Not Found.

Testcase Objective: Verify a user with correct username and password is authenticated and reaches the home page.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter a valid, active username | 3. Enter the correct password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: AuthProviderChain authenticates via LocalAuthProvider, AuthUser is marked authenticated, a LoginLog record is created, and the user is redirected to the application home page.

Testcase Objective: Verify login is rejected when the password does not match the stored credentials.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter a valid username | 3. Enter an incorrect password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: AuthenticationService::setCredentials fails, AuthenticationException::invalidCredentials is thrown, generic 'Invalid credentials' flash message is shown, user remains on login page unauthenticated.

Testcase Objective: Verify login with an unregistered username returns the same generic error as a wrong password (no user enumeration).
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter a username that does not exist | 3. Enter any password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: getCredentials returns no user, invalid_credentials error is shown; message text is identical to the wrong-password case, preventing username enumeration.

Testcase Objective: Verify submitting the login form without a username is handled as invalid credentials.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Leave username blank | 3. Enter a password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: Request is processed with username='' ; no matching user is found; invalid_credentials error is returned and shown on the login page.

Testcase Objective: Verify submitting the login form without a password is handled as invalid credentials.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter a valid username | 3. Leave password blank | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: Credential match fails for blank password; invalid_credentials error is returned and shown on the login page.

Testcase Name: Login with both username and password empty
Testcase Objective: Verify submitting a completely empty login form does not authenticate the user.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Leave both fields blank | 3. Click Login
Expected Result: UserCredential is created with empty strings, authentication fails, invalid_credentials error shown, no session is created.

Testcase Name: SQL injection attempt in username field
Testcase Objective: Verify a SQL-injection style payload in the username field cannot bypass authentication.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter a payload such as admin' OR '1'='1 in username | 3. Enter any password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: ORM/DAO uses parameterised queries; no user matches the payload; invalid_credentials error is returned; no unauthorized access or SQL error is exposed.

Testcase Name: Already authenticated user requests the login page
Testcase Objective: Verify a user who already has an authenticated session is redirected away from the login form instead of seeing it again.
Steps: 1. Log in successfully | 2. While the session is still active, navigate directly to /auth/login again
Expected Result: LoginController::handle detects AuthUser::isAuthenticated()=true and redirects to the home page path instead of rendering the login form.

Testcase Name: Root URL redirects to login page
Testcase Objective: Verify hitting the application root path redirects an unauthenticated visitor to the login page.
Steps: 1. Clear any session/cookies | 2. Navigate to the application root URL (/)
Expected Result: RootController::handle issues a redirect to auth/login.

Testcase Name: Unexpected error during authentication is handled gracefully
Testcase Objective: Verify that an unexpected (non-AuthenticationException) failure during the authentication chain does not crash the login flow.
Steps: 1. Trigger a condition that causes an unhandled Throwable during authenticate() (e.g. simulated backend failure) | 2. Submit valid-looking login credentials
Expected Result: The generic catch(Throwable) block in ValidateController sets an 'Unexpected error occurred' flash message and redirects back to the login page instead of exposing a stack trace.

Testcase Name: Successful login is recorded in the login log
Testcase Objective: Verify a successful authentication creates an accurate entry in the login log (ohrm_login).
Steps: 1. Log in successfully as a known user | 2. Inspect the ohrm_login table/LoginLog records for the session
Expected Result: LoginService::addLogin persists a LoginLog row with the correct user id, username, user role name and whether the role is predefined.

Testcase Name: Login form renders CSRF token and provider options correctly
Testcase Objective: Verify the login page pre-render step supplies a CSRF token and the configured social/OpenID login provider list.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login (unauthenticated) | 2. Inspect the rendered auth-login component props
Expected Result: A unique 'login' CSRF token is present, and the authenticators prop lists the configured OpenID providers (empty array if none configured).

Testcase Objective: Verify clicking Logout ends the current authenticated session and returns the user to the login page.
Steps: 1. Log in successfully | 2. Click Logout / navigate to auth/logout
Expected Result: LogoutController invalidates the Session and issues a redirect to auth/login.

Testcase Name: Protected pages are inaccessible immediately after logout
Testcase Objective: Verify that after logout, previously accessible authenticated pages can no longer be reached without logging in again.
Steps: 1. Log in and open a protected page (e.g. dashboard) | 2. Logout | 3. Use browser back button or re-navigate to the same protected URL
Expected Result: AuthenticationSubscriber detects the user is no longer authenticated and forces a redirect/SessionExpiredException back to the login page; protected content is not shown.

Testcase Objective: Verify hitting the logout endpoint without an existing session does not error out.
Steps: 1. Ensure no active session/cookies exist | 2. Navigate directly to auth/logout
Expected Result: Session::invalidate() is called safely and the user is redirected to auth/login without an application error.

Testcase Name: Logout endpoint does not require a CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify current behaviour: LogoutController performs no CSRF token validation before invalidating the session, which means logout can be triggered cross-site (documenting current behaviour/gap, not a confirmed protection).
Steps: 1. Log in successfully | 2. From a third-party page/context, issue a GET request to auth/logout without any _token parameter
Expected Result: The session is invalidated and the browser is redirected to auth/login with no CSRF check performed - confirms no CSRF protection exists on logout in current code.

Testcase Name: Request reset code with a valid, active registered username
Testcase Objective: Verify a valid active user with an assigned employee and work email successfully triggers a password reset email.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode | 2. Enter a valid, active username | 3. Submit the form
Expected Result: searchForUserRecord finds the user, logPasswordResetRequest generates a reset code, sends an email to the employee's work email, and the user is redirected to auth/sendPasswordReset (success page).

Testcase Name: Request reset code with an unknown/non-existent username
Testcase Objective: Verify that requesting a reset for a username that does not exist does not reveal whether the account exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode | 2. Enter a username that does not exist | 3. Submit the form
Expected Result: searchForUserRecord returns null; the controller still redirects to auth/sendPasswordReset (the same success page as a valid request), so the response does not disclose that the username is invalid.

Testcase Name: Request reset code for a disabled user account
Testcase Objective: Verify a disabled account's owner cannot be distinguished from a valid request via the response, and no email is sent.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode | 2. Enter the username of a disabled user account | 3. Submit the form
Expected Result: searchForUserRecord returns null because !$user->getStatus(); no email is sent; user is still redirected to the generic success page (anti-enumeration).

Testcase Name: Request reset code for a terminated employee's account
Testcase Objective: Verify a terminated employee's account cannot be used to trigger a password reset email, without exposing that fact.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode | 2. Enter the username tied to a terminated employee | 3. Submit the form
Expected Result: searchForUserRecord returns null (EmployeeTerminationRecord present); no email sent; generic success redirect shown.

Testcase Name: Request reset code for a user with no work email configured
Testcase Objective: Verify a user whose employee record has no work email cannot complete the reset flow, without exposing that fact.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode | 2. Enter the username of a user whose employee has no work email set | 3. Submit the form
Expected Result: searchForUserRecord returns null (empty work email); no email is sent; generic success redirect is still shown.

Testcase Name: Request reset code with missing CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the reset request form rejects submissions without a valid 'request-reset-password' CSRF token.
Steps: 1. Submit the forgot-password form with the _token field removed
Expected Result: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('request-reset-password', null) fails; AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken is thrown.

Testcase Name: Request reset code with an invalid/tampered CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the reset request form rejects a forged or expired CSRF token value.
Steps: 1. Submit the forgot-password form with an arbitrary/incorrect _token value
Expected Result: Token validation fails and AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken is thrown before any user lookup occurs.

Testcase Name: Forgot password page shown when email is not configured
Testcase Objective: Verify the request-password page displays an email configuration warning instead of the reset form when SMTP/email is not set up.
Steps: 1. Ensure EmailService::isConfigSet() is false (no email config) | 2. Navigate to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode
Expected Result: RequestPasswordController::preRender renders the 'email-configuration-warning' component instead of 'request-reset-password'.

Testcase Name: Reset email fails to send due to invalid/malicious recipient address
Testcase Objective: Verify a work email that fails validation or contains header-injection characters blocks the reset email and routes to the failure page.
Steps: 1. Configure/target an employee whose work email is malformed or contains a CR/LF header-injection sequence | 2. Submit a reset request for that username
Expected Result: sendPasswordResetCodeEmail rejects the address via filter_var/regex checks (leading '-' or \r\n), returns false, and RequestResetPasswordController redirects to auth/sendPasswordResetFailure.

Testcase Name: Reset request success and failure pages render the correct components
Testcase Objective: Verify the dedicated success and failure landing pages render their respective Vue components.
Steps: 1. Trigger a successful reset request and observe auth/sendPasswordReset | 2. Trigger a failed reset request (e.g. email send failure) and observe auth/sendPasswordResetFailure
Expected Result: RequestPasswordSuccessController renders 'reset-password-success'; RequestPasswordFailureController renders 'reset-password-failure'.

Testcase Name: Multiple consecutive reset requests for the same user
Testcase Objective: Verify requesting a new reset code before using a previous one is accepted and generates a fresh code (current behaviour, no throttling found in code).
Steps: 1. Submit a valid reset request for a username | 2. Immediately submit a second reset request for the same username
Expected Result: Two ResetPasswordRequest rows are created; a new reset code/email is generated each time; no rate limiting or cooldown is enforced in ResetPasswordService/ResetPasswordDao.

Testcase Name: Open reset link with a valid, unused, unexpired code
Testcase Objective: Verify a valid reset link renders the reset-password form pre-filled with the correct username.
Steps: 1. Request a password reset for a valid user | 2. Open the emailed reset link (auth/resetPassword/resetCode/{code})
Expected Result: ResetPasswordService::validateUrl resolves the user; ResetCodeController renders the 'reset-password' component with username, code, and a 'reset-password' CSRF token.

Testcase Name: Submit a new password with a valid code and matching username
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can successfully set a new password through a valid reset link.
Steps: 1. Open a valid reset link | 2. Enter the matching username and a compliant new password | 3. Submit
Expected Result: saveResetPassword updates the user's password, updateResetPasswordValid marks the request as used (expired=0), the session is invalidated, and the user is redirected to auth/login.

Testcase Name: Open reset link with an invalid/non-existent code
Testcase Objective: Verify a bogus reset code shows an error state rather than a reset form.
Steps: 1. Navigate to auth/resetPassword/resetCode/{randomInvalidCode}
Expected Result: getResetPasswordLogByResetCode finds no matching request; ResetCodeController renders the 'reset-password-error' component.

Testcase Name: Open reset link after it has expired (older than 1 day)
Testcase Objective: Verify a reset code becomes unusable once more than one day has elapsed since it was requested.
Steps: 1. Generate a reset code | 2. Wait until hasPasswordResetRequestNotExpired(request) > 0 (more than 1 day elapsed), or manipulate resetRequestDate | 3. Open the reset link
Expected Result: validateUrl detects the elapsed day count > 0 and returns null; the reset-password-error page is shown.

Testcase Name: Reuse an older reset code after a newer one was requested
Testcase Objective: Verify that once a new reset code is requested for the same email, the previous code is no longer accepted (replay of a stale code).
Steps: 1. Request a password reset (code A) | 2. Request a second password reset for the same account (code B) | 3. Open the link containing code A
Expected Result: validateUrl compares code A against the latest stored reset code for that email (code B) via getResetPasswordLogByEmail; since they differ, code A is rejected as 'old one & not valid'.

Testcase Name: Reuse a reset code after it has already been used
Testcase Objective: Verify a reset code cannot be used a second time to change the password again.
Steps: 1. Successfully complete a password reset using a valid code | 2. Re-open/resubmit the same reset link
Expected Result: updateResetPasswordValid already set expired=0 for that email; validateUrl's !$resetPassword->getExpired() check now evaluates true, so the code is treated as expired/invalid and rejected.

Testcase Name: Submit reset password with a username that does not match the reset code owner
Testcase Objective: Verify the reset form rejects a username that does not belong to the resolved reset code.
Steps: 1. Open a valid reset link for user A | 2. Edit/submit the form with a different username, e.g. user B | 3. Submit
Expected Result: ResetPasswordController compares $user->getUserName() to the submitted username; on mismatch it throws AuthenticationException::invalidResetCode.

Testcase Name: Submit reset password form with missing or invalid CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the reset-password form enforces CSRF protection.
Steps: 1. Open a valid reset link | 2. Submit the form with the _token field removed or altered
Expected Result: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('reset-password', token) fails; AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken is thrown before the password is changed.

Testcase Name: Submit a weak/non-compliant new password via reset password form
Testcase Objective: Verify whether the reset-password flow enforces the configured password strength policy before saving (documents current behaviour/possible gap).
Steps: 1. Open a valid reset link | 2. Enter a very short/weak password (e.g. '1234') as the new password | 3. Submit
Expected Result: ResetPasswordController::handle calls saveResetPassword directly with no PasswordStrengthService/PasswordStrengthValidation check in this controller; verify whether the weak password is accepted (current code path does not call the strength validator here) - flag as a gap if it is accepted.

Testcase Name: Successful password reset invalidates the current session
Testcase Objective: Verify that completing a reset forces any existing session to end, requiring fresh login with the new password.
Steps: 1. While logged in on Browser A, complete a password reset for the same account on Browser B | 2. Interact with Browser A
Expected Result: ResetPasswordController::handle calls $session->invalidate() after saving the new password; Browser A's session is no longer valid on the next request.

Testcase Name: Login succeeds but password fails the strength policy while enforcement is on
Testcase Objective: Verify a technically-correct login is intercepted and redirected to forced password reset when the password does not meet the configured strength policy.
Steps: 1. Ensure config auth.password_policy.enforce_password_strength = 'on' | 2. Log in with correct credentials for a password that fails isValidPassword() | 3. Observe redirect
Expected Result: LocalAuthProvider throws PasswordEnforceException, invalidates the session, generates an enforce-password reset code, and ValidateController redirects to changeWeakPassword/resetCode/{code} instead of the home page.

Testcase Name: Weak password reset page loads with a valid reset code
Testcase Objective: Verify the forced reset page correctly identifies the user and renders the change-password form.
Steps: 1. Trigger the weak-password flow to obtain a reset code | 2. Open /auth/changeWeakPassword/resetCode/{code}
Expected Result: PasswordStrengthService::validateUrl returns true; WeakPasswordResetController renders 'reset-weak-password' with username, code, and a 'reset-weak-password' CSRF token.

Testcase Name: Weak password reset page with an invalid or already-used code
Testcase Objective: Verify an invalid enforce-password reset code shows the invalid-code state rather than the form.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/changeWeakPassword/resetCode/{invalidOrUsedCode}
Expected Result: validateUrl returns false (no matching record or isExpired()=true); the component receives invalid-code=true and does not expose the change-password fields.

Testcase Name: Enforce-password reset code expires after 1 hour
Testcase Objective: Verify an enforce-password reset code becomes invalid once more than one hour has passed since the request.
Steps: 1. Trigger the weak-password flow to obtain a reset code | 2. Wait over 1 hour (or adjust resetRequestDate) so dateDiffInHours > 1 | 3. Open the reset link
Expected Result: isResetCodeTimeOut returns true; validateUrl marks the request updateEnforcedPasswordValid(...,true) and returns false, showing the invalid-code state.

Testcase Name: Submit a strong new password with the correct current password
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can successfully replace a weak password with a compliant one via the forced-reset form.
Steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link | 2. Enter the correct current password | 3. Enter a new password meeting all policy rules | 4. Submit
Expected Result: isCurrentPassword validates the current password, saveEnforcedPassword updates the password and marks the enforce request as used (expired=true), and the user is redirected to auth/login.

Testcase Name: Submit the forced-reset form with an incorrect current password
Testcase Objective: Verify the forced-reset flow rejects an incorrect current password.
Steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link | 2. Enter a wrong current password | 3. Enter any new password | 4. Submit
Expected Result: isCurrentPassword returns false; a FLASH_PASSWORD_ENFORCE_ERROR with 'invalid_credentials' is set and the user is redirected back to the same reset page with an error shown.

Testcase Name: Submit the forced-reset form with missing/invalid CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the forced password reset form enforces CSRF protection.
Steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link | 2. Submit the form with the _token removed or altered
Expected Result: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('reset-weak-password', token) fails; a FLASH_PASSWORD_ENFORCE_ERROR 'invalid_csrf_token' is set and the user is redirected back to the same page.

Testcase Name: Submit a new password that still fails the strength policy
Testcase Objective: Verify the forced-reset endpoint blocks a replacement password that still does not satisfy the configured complexity rules.
Steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link | 2. Enter the correct current password | 3. Enter a new password that is still weak (e.g. missing a special character) | 4. Submit
Expected Result: validateParameters() re-checks isValidPassword() and returns false; RequestResetWeakPasswordController::handleBadRequest() is returned, the password is not saved.

Testcase Name: Reuse an enforce-password reset code after it has already been consumed
Testcase Objective: Verify a completed enforce-password reset code cannot be replayed to change the password again.
Steps: 1. Successfully complete a forced password reset using a code | 2. Re-submit the same reset code/form
Expected Result: The EnforcePasswordRequest was marked expired=true by updateEnforcedPasswordValid; a subsequent validateUrl call returns false because isExpired() is true.

Testcase Name: Username and password field length boundaries on the forced-reset form
Testcase Objective: Verify the forced-reset endpoint enforces username length (5-40 chars) and password max length (64 chars) parameter rules.
Steps: 1. Submit the forced-reset form with a username of 4 characters (below USERNAME_MIN_LENGTH) | 2. Repeat with a password longer than 64 characters (MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH)
Expected Result: ParamRuleCollection LENGTH rules fail validation in validateParameters(); the request is rejected via handleBadRequest() rather than being processed.

Testcase Name: Password satisfies all configured policy rules
Testcase Objective: Verify a password meeting length, character-class and strength requirements passes validation with no messages.
Steps: 1. Call POST /api/v2/auth/validation/password (or trigger via reset form) with a password of length >= 8 containing upper, lower, digit, special char, no spaces, and a strong zxcvbn score | 2. Inspect the response
Expected Result: checkPasswordPolicies returns an empty messages array and isValidPassword returns true; API returns strength score with no warning messages.

Testcase Name: Password shorter than the minimum length (7 characters)
