Testcase Objective: Verify a password below the configured minimum length (default 8) is flagged.
Steps: 1. Submit a 7-character password for validation
Expected Result: checkMinPasswordLength returns true; the 'auth.password_min_length' message is included and isValidPassword returns false.

Testcase Name: Password exactly at the minimum length boundary (8 characters)
Testcase Objective: Verify a password exactly at the configured minimum length is accepted (when all other rules are satisfied).
Steps: 1. Submit an 8-character password that also satisfies upper/lower/number/special-char/no-space rules
Expected Result: checkMinPasswordLength returns false (8 is not < 8); no min-length message is generated.

Testcase Name: Password exceeding the maximum length (65 characters)
Testcase Objective: Verify a password longer than MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH (64) is flagged.
Steps: 1. Submit a 65-character password for validation
Expected Result: checkMaxPasswordLength returns true; the 'auth.password_max_length' message is included and isValidPassword returns false.

Testcase Name: Password exactly at the maximum length boundary (64 characters)
Testcase Objective: Verify a password exactly at MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH is accepted.
Steps: 1. Submit a 64-character password satisfying all other rules
Expected Result: checkMaxPasswordLength returns false (64 is not > 64); no max-length message is generated.

Testcase Objective: Verify a password with zero uppercase letters is rejected when the policy requires at least one.
Steps: 1. Submit a password containing only lowercase letters, digits and special characters
Expected Result: checkMinUppercaseLetters returns true; the 'auth.password_n_uppercase_letters' message is returned.

Testcase Objective: Verify a password with zero lowercase letters is rejected when the policy requires at least one.
Steps: 1. Submit a password containing only uppercase letters, digits and special characters
Expected Result: checkMinLowercaseLetters returns true; the 'auth.password_n_lowercase_letters' message is returned.

Testcase Objective: Verify a password with no digits is rejected when the policy requires at least one number.
Steps: 1. Submit a password containing only letters and special characters
Expected Result: checkMinNumbersInPassword returns true; the 'auth.password_n_numbers' message is returned.

Testcase Objective: Verify a password with no special characters is rejected when the policy requires at least one.
Steps: 1. Submit a password containing only letters and digits
Expected Result: checkMinSpecialCharacters returns true; the 'auth.password_n_special_characters' message is returned.

Testcase Name: Password containing spaces when spaces are disallowed
Testcase Objective: Verify a password containing whitespace is rejected under the default is_spaces_allowed=false policy.
Steps: 1. Submit a password containing a space character, e.g. 'Str0ng Pass!'
Expected Result: checkSpacesInPassword returns true; the 'auth.password_spaces_not_allowed' message is returned.

Testcase Name: Common/guessable password that satisfies character-class rules but has low entropy
Testcase Objective: Verify a predictable password (e.g. 'Password1!') that technically satisfies length/character rules is still flagged as guessable via the zxcvbn strength score.
Steps: 1. Submit a common/predictable password like 'Password1!' that meets length and character-class rules | 2. Inspect the strength score and messages
Expected Result: PasswordStrengthValidation::checkPasswordStrength scores it below the configured default_required_password_strength ('strong'); checkRequiredDefaultPasswordStrength returns true and the 'auth.password_could_be_guessable' message is added since no other messages exist.

Testcase Name: Login form submitted with a missing CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the login POST is rejected when _token is absent.
Steps: 1. Submit the login form (ValidateController) with the _token field stripped out
Expected Result: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('login', null) returns false; AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken is thrown, caught, and the user is redirected to the login page with an error flash before any credential check occurs.

Testcase Name: Login form submitted with an invalid/tampered CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the login POST is rejected when _token does not match the session-issued token.
Steps: 1. Submit the login form with a random/incorrect _token value and otherwise-valid credentials
Expected Result: Token validation fails first; invalid_csrf_token error is shown even though the credentials themselves were correct.

Testcase Objective: Verify the forgot-password request form is protected against CSRF.
Steps: 1. Submit the request-reset-password form with _token removed
Expected Result: RequestResetPasswordController throws AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken before searching for the user.

Testcase Name: Reset-password form missing or invalid CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the final reset-password submission form is protected against CSRF.
Steps: 1. Submit the reset-password form (valid reset code) with _token removed or altered
Expected Result: ResetPasswordController throws AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken before the new password is saved.

Testcase Name: Reset-weak-password form missing or invalid CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the forced weak-password reset form is protected against CSRF.
Steps: 1. Submit the reset-weak-password form with _token removed or altered
Expected Result: isValid('reset-weak-password', token) fails; a FLASH_PASSWORD_ENFORCE_ERROR invalid_csrf_token is set and the user is redirected back without the password being changed.

Testcase Name: Administrator-access verification form missing or invalid CSRF token
Testcase Objective: Verify the step-up admin verification form is protected against CSRF.
Steps: 1. Submit the administrator-access verification form with _token removed or altered, using a correct admin password
Expected Result: AdministratorVerifyController throws AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken even though the password was correct; FLASH_VERIFY_ERROR is set and the user is forwarded back to the verification page.

Testcase Name: Token issued for one form cannot validate a different form
Testcase Objective: Verify each form uses a distinct CSRF token namespace (id) so a token cannot be replayed across unrelated forms.
Steps: 1. Capture the CSRF token rendered on the login page ('login' id) | 2. Attempt to submit the reset-password form using that token value as _token
Expected Result: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('reset-password', loginToken) returns false because the token id differs, so validation fails.

Testcase Name: A fresh, unique CSRF token is issued on every relevant page load
Testcase Objective: Verify token freshness/uniqueness so tokens are not trivially predictable or globally shared.
Steps: 1. Load the login page twice in separate sessions | 2. Compare the rendered 'token' prop values
Expected Result: Each session receives its own token value bound to that session's TokenStorage, per Symfony CsrfTokenManager semantics.

Testcase Name: Expired session token replay after logout
Testcase Objective: Verify a CSRF token captured before logout cannot be used to perform a state-changing action after the session ends.
Steps: 1. Log in and capture the login page's CSRF token | 2. Logout | 3. Attempt to submit an authenticated form action using the captured token
Expected Result: Because the session/token storage was invalidated on logout, the previously captured token no longer validates against the new session state.

Testcase Name: User without admin-verify permission is forwarded to Forbidden page
Testcase Objective: Verify a user lacking the 'auth_admin_verify' data-group read permission cannot reach the admin verification step.
Steps: 1. Log in as a user/role without permission on data group 'auth_admin_verify' | 2. Trigger an action that invokes AdministratorVerifyController
Expected Result: getDataGroupPermissions('auth_admin_verify')->canRead() is false; a RequestForwardableException forwards the request to ForbiddenController, rendering the 403 'auth-forbidden' page.

Testcase Name: Authorized admin submits correct password on the verification page
Testcase Objective: Verify a permitted user can step up to admin access by re-entering their password correctly.
Steps: 1. Navigate to an admin-privileged action, triggering the Administrator Access page | 2. Enter the correct account password | 3. Submit
Expected Result: AuthenticationService::setCredentials succeeds; AuthUser::setHasAdminAccess(true) is set, the login is logged, and the user is forwarded to the originally requested (forward) URL.

Testcase Name: Authorized admin submits an incorrect password on the verification page
Testcase Objective: Verify re-authentication fails safely when the wrong password is supplied on the step-up form.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the Administrator Access page | 2. Enter an incorrect password | 3. Submit
Expected Result: setCredentials returns false, AuthenticationException::invalidCredentials is thrown, FLASH_VERIFY_ERROR is set, and the user is forwarded back to AdministratorAccessController with the error shown; hasAdminAccess remains false.

Testcase Name: Admin access flag is not sticky across page navigation
Testcase Objective: Verify that gaining admin access on one page does not silently grant it on subsequent unrelated pages, per AdministratorAccessSubscriber.
Steps: 1. Successfully verify admin access for one privileged action | 2. Navigate to a different Vue-rendered controller that does not implement AdminPrivilegeController
Expected Result: AdministratorAccessSubscriber::onControllerEvent resets AuthUser::setHasAdminAccess(false) for any AbstractVueController that is not an instance of AdminPrivilegeController, forcing re-verification for the next privileged action.

Testcase Name: Administrator Access page respects the 'forward' query parameter
Testcase Objective: Verify the intended destination after verification is captured from the 'forward' query string.
Steps: 1. Navigate to auth/admin/access?forward=/some/admin/path
Expected Result: The forward URL is stored on AuthUser::ADMIN_ACCESS_FORWARD_URL and used to redirect after a successful verification.

Testcase Name: Administrator Access page falls back to the home page as the back URL
Testcase Objective: Verify that without an explicit 'back' query parameter (and no prior flash error), the back-url defaults to the user's home page path.
Steps: 1. Navigate directly to the Administrator Access page with no 'back' query parameter and no pending FLASH_VERIFY_ERROR
Expected Result: backUrl is computed as '/' + HomePageService::getHomePagePath() and passed to the component as the 'back-url' prop.

Testcase Name: Forward/back session attributes are cleared after successful verification
Testcase Objective: Verify stale forward/back URLs do not leak into subsequent unrelated privileged actions.
Steps: 1. Successfully complete admin verification with a forward URL set | 2. Inspect AuthUser attributes afterward
Expected Result: AdministratorVerifyController removes ADMIN_ACCESS_FORWARD_URL and ADMIN_ACCESS_BACK_URL from AuthUser after a successful redirect.

Testcase Name: Terminated or disabled admin user cannot pass step-up verification
Testcase Objective: Verify that even with the correct password, a disabled or terminated admin account fails the re-authentication check.
Steps: 1. As a disabled or terminated admin user with an existing session, trigger the Administrator Access verification | 2. Enter the correct (still valid) password | 3. Submit
Expected Result: AuthenticationService::setCredentialsForUser throws userDisabled/employeeTerminated before hasAdminAccess can be set to true; verification fails.

Testcase Name: Forbidden page renders the correct 403 component
Testcase Objective: Verify the Forbidden landing page displays the expected UI when access is denied.
Steps: 1. Trigger any RequestForwardableException route to ForbiddenController (e.g. lacking admin_verify permission)
Expected Result: ForbiddenController::preRender renders the 'auth-forbidden' Vue component with an HTTP 403 status.

Testcase Name: Session times out while browsing an authenticated view page
Testcase Objective: Verify an expired/invalidated session on a standard (view) controller redirects the user to the login page instead of showing stale content.
Steps: 1. Log in | 2. Force the session to become unauthenticated (e.g. expire it server-side) | 3. Navigate to any authenticated view page
Expected Result: AuthenticationSubscriber::onControllerEvent detects the controller is not PublicControllerInterface, throws SessionExpiredException, and onExceptionEvent redirects to auth/login.

Testcase Name: Session times out during a REST API call
Testcase Objective: Verify an expired session hitting a REST endpoint returns a structured 401 instead of an HTML redirect.
Steps: 1. Log in and obtain a session | 2. Invalidate/expire the session | 3. Call any authenticated REST V2 API endpoint
Expected Result: AuthenticationSubscriber throws UnauthorizedException carrying an HTTP 401 JSON error body ('Session expired'); onExceptionEvent returns that response directly.

Testcase Name: Account is disabled by an admin while the user has an active session
Testcase Objective: Verify a mid-session account disable takes effect on the very next request rather than waiting for re-login.
Steps: 1. Log in as user X in Session A | 2. In a separate admin session, disable user X's account | 3. Perform any action in Session A
Expected Result: resolveAuthenticatedUserException detects isLoggedInUserActive()=false, logoutCurrentSession invalidates the session and sets a 'user_disabled' flash message; the user is forced back to the login page.

Testcase Name: Employee is terminated while the user has an active session
Testcase Objective: Verify a mid-session employee termination immediately revokes access.
Steps: 1. Log in as user X in an active session | 2. Terminate the associated employee record | 3. Perform any subsequent action
Expected Result: resolveAuthenticatedUserException detects the EmployeeTerminationRecord and forces a logout with an 'employee_terminated' message.

Testcase Name: User record is modified elsewhere, invalidating the current session token
Testcase Objective: Verify that if the logged-in user's dateModified timestamp changes (e.g. edited by an admin) the current session is treated as stale and ended.
Steps: 1. Log in as user X | 2. Have an admin modify user X's record (changing dateModified) | 3. Perform any subsequent action as user X in the original session
Expected Result: hasUserLastModifiedChanged returns true; a 'session_expired' AuthenticationException triggers logoutCurrentSession, forcing re-login.

Testcase Name: Re-login after session timeout returns the user to the originally requested page
Testcase Objective: Verify the post-timeout login flow restores the user's original destination rather than always going to the home page.
Steps: 1. Attempt to open a deep-linked authenticated page while the session is expired (captures SESSION_TIMEOUT_REDIRECT_URL) | 2. Log back in successfully
Expected Result: handleSessionTimeoutRedirect reads and clears AuthUser::SESSION_TIMEOUT_REDIRECT_URL and ValidateController redirects there instead of the default home page, provided it differs from the login/logout URLs.

Testcase Name: Public authentication pages remain reachable without a session
Testcase Objective: Verify login, forgot-password and reset-password pages are excluded from the session-expiry enforcement.
Steps: 1. With no active session, navigate to /auth/login, /auth/requestPasswordResetCode, and a valid /auth/resetPassword/resetCode/{code} link
Expected Result: Each controller implements PublicControllerInterface; AuthenticationSubscriber::onControllerEvent returns early for these routes without throwing SessionExpiredException.

Testcase Name: Unauthenticated request to a protected page never exposes protected content
Testcase Objective: Verify an unauthenticated user hitting a non-public controller is always intercepted before any business content renders.
Steps: 1. With no session/cookies, navigate directly to a known authenticated-only URL
Expected Result: onRequestEvent stops propagation since isAuthenticated() is false, and onControllerEvent subsequently throws SessionExpiredException (or 401 for REST), so protected data is never rendered.

Testcase Name: Login attempt with a disabled user account and correct password
Testcase Objective: Verify a disabled account cannot log in even when the password is correct, and receives a specific message.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter the username of a disabled account | 3. Enter the correct password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: setCredentialsForUser detects !$user->getStatus() and throws AuthenticationException::userDisabled ('Account disabled'); login is refused.

Testcase Name: Login attempt with a terminated employee's user account
Testcase Objective: Verify an account belonging to a terminated employee cannot log in even with correct credentials.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter the username tied to a terminated employee | 3. Enter the correct password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: setCredentialsForUser detects an EmployeeTerminationRecord and throws AuthenticationException::employeeTerminated ('Employee is terminated'); login is refused.

Testcase Name: Login attempt with a user account that has no linked employee
Testcase Objective: Verify a system user account without an associated employee record cannot complete login.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter the username of a user with empNumber = null | 3. Enter the correct password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: setCredentialsForUser throws AuthenticationException::employeeNotAssigned ('Employee not assigned'); login is refused.

Testcase Name: Login attempt with a deleted user account
Testcase Objective: Verify a soft-deleted user account is rejected with the generic invalid-credentials message rather than a specific status message.
Steps: 1. Navigate to /auth/login | 2. Enter the username of a user where isDeleted()=true | 3. Enter any password | 4. Click Login
Expected Result: setCredentialsForUser returns false immediately for a deleted user (no specific exception), so AuthProviderChain reports failure and ValidateController shows the generic invalid_credentials message - distinct from the disabled/terminated messaging.

Testcase Name: Forced password-save flows reject disabled/terminated users at the final save step
Testcase Objective: Verify that even if a reset/enforce-password code is otherwise valid, the underlying save is blocked for a disabled or terminated account.
Steps: 1. Obtain a valid reset-password or enforce-password reset code for a user | 2. Disable the user's account or terminate their employee record before completing the reset | 3. Submit the new password
Expected Result: ResetPasswordService::validateUser / PasswordStrengthService's user validation reject the account (returns null for a terminated employee), so saveResetPassword/saveEnforcedPassword does not update the credentials.

Testcase Name: Previously issued reset links become unusable once the account is disabled mid-flow
Testcase Objective: Verify a reset code requested while the account was active cannot be exploited after the account is disabled before the code is used.
Steps: 1. Request a password reset for an active account (obtain code) | 2. Disable the account before the code is used | 3. Attempt to complete the reset using the code
Expected Result: validateUser in ResetPasswordService checks the employee's termination status at save time; combined with searchForUserRecord's status checks at request time, a disabled account cannot have its password changed via a stale link.

Testcase Name: No lockout after repeated failed login attempts
Testcase Objective: Document current behaviour: verify whether the application locks or throttles an account after multiple consecutive failed login attempts.
Steps: 1. Attempt to log in with a valid username and an incorrect password 10+ times in quick succession | 2. Attempt login again with the correct password
Expected Result: No brute-force lockout, delay, or CAPTCHA mechanism was found in LocalAuthProvider/AuthenticationService/ValidateController; the correct-password attempt succeeds immediately afterward, confirming no rate limiting is currently implemented (gap, not a verified protection).

Testcase Name: Error messages differentiate account-status reasons but not username validity
Testcase Objective: Verify that while wrong-password and unknown-username both return a generic message, disabled/terminated/unassigned states return distinct messages that could allow limited account-status enumeration.
Steps: 1. Attempt login against a non-existent username | 2. Attempt login against a known-disabled username with any password | 3. Attempt login against a known-terminated-employee username with any password | 4. Compare the three error messages
Expected Result: Steps 1 uses the generic 'invalid_credentials' message, while steps 2 and 3 return distinct 'user_disabled' / 'employee_terminated' messages - confirming an attacker could infer that a disabled/terminated username exists, unlike a wrong password or unknown username.

Testcase Name: Verify comment count increments correctly with multiple comments
Testcase Objective: Verify the post's number-of-comments counter increases correctly with each new comment added.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Open a post with 0 comments | 3. Add 3 separate comments | 4. Refresh the post view
Expected Result: Comment count on the post displays 3 and all 3 comments are listed.

Testcase Name: Edit own comment with valid text
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can edit the text of their own comment.
Steps: 1. Login as comment author | 2. Open the post containing own comment | 3. Click Edit on the comment | 4. Update the text | 5. Save changes
Expected Result: Comment text is updated successfully and displayed with the updated content.

Testcase Name: Attempt to edit another employee's comment
Testcase Objective: Verify a regular ESS user cannot edit a comment authored by another employee.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user A | 2. Call PUT /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments/{commentId} for a comment authored by employee B | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 403 Forbidden and the comment remains unchanged.

Testcase Name: Edit comment with text exceeding max length
Testcase Objective: Verify system rejects edited comment text exceeding the 65530 character limit.
Steps: 1. Login as comment author | 2. Edit own comment | 3. Enter text of 65531 characters | 4. Save changes
Expected Result: Validation error is returned and comment is not updated.

Testcase Name: Edit a comment that does not exist
Testcase Objective: Verify system returns a not-found error when editing a comment ID that does not exist.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call PUT /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments/99999999 with valid text | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns a 404 Record Not Found error.

Testcase Objective: Verify a user can delete their own comment from a post.
Steps: 1. Login as comment author | 2. Open the post containing own comment | 3. Click Delete on the comment | 4. Confirm deletion
Expected Result: Comment is removed and the post's comment count decreases by 1.

Testcase Name: Attempt to delete another employee's comment
Testcase Objective: Verify a regular ESS user cannot delete a comment authored by another employee.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user A | 2. Call DELETE /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments/{commentId} for a comment authored by employee B | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 403 Forbidden and the comment is not deleted.

Testcase Name: Delete a comment that does not exist
Testcase Objective: Verify system returns a not-found error when deleting a non-existent comment ID.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call DELETE /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments/99999999 | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns a 404 Record Not Found error.

Testcase Objective: Verify a user with admin-level Buzz comment permissions can delete any employee's comment.
Steps: 1. Login as Admin | 2. Open a post containing another employee's comment | 3. Click Delete on that comment | 4. Confirm deletion
Expected Result: Comment is deleted successfully and comment count decreases by 1, regardless of ownership.

Testcase Name: List all comments on a post in chronological order
Testcase Objective: Verify comments on a post are listed sorted by creation time (comment.createdAtUtc).
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments | 3. Inspect order of returned comments
Expected Result: Comments are returned in order of createdAtUtc with the correct total count.

Testcase Name: Paginate comments list using limit and offset
Testcase Objective: Verify the comments list supports pagination.
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments?limit=2&offset=0 | 2. Call the same endpoint with offset=2 | 3. Compare results
Expected Result: Each call returns a distinct page of up to 2 comments and meta.total reflects the full comment count.

Testcase Name: List comments with detailed model parameter
Testcase Objective: Verify comments can be retrieved using the detailed model returning extended comment information.
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/comments?model=detailed | 2. Inspect response structure
Expected Result: Response returns comments in the detailed BuzzDetailedCommentModel format including additional metadata such as like status.

Testcase Name: Like a post for the first time
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can like a Buzz post/share that they have not previously liked.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Open the Buzz feed | 3. Click the Like button on a post not yet liked by the user | 4. Observe result
Expected Result: Like is registered, the post's like count increases by 1, and the Like button changes to a Liked state.

Testcase Name: Attempt to like a post that is already liked
Testcase Objective: Verify system prevents a user from liking the same post twice.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who has already liked a post | 2. Call POST /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/likes again for the same post | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 400 Bad Request with message Already liked and the like count does not increase further.

Testcase Objective: Verify a user can remove their like from a post they previously liked.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who has liked a post | 2. Click the Unlike/Liked button on that post | 3. Observe result
Expected Result: Like is removed, the post's like count decreases by 1, and the button reverts to a Like state.

Testcase Name: Attempt to unlike a post that was never liked
Testcase Objective: Verify system rejects an unlike request for a post the user has not liked.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who has not liked a specific post | 2. Call DELETE /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/likes | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 400 Bad Request with message Not previously liked and no changes occur.

Testcase Name: List all users who liked a post
Testcase Objective: Verify the list of likes for a given post/share can be retrieved.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/shares/{shareId}/likes | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: Response returns the list of employees who liked the post along with the total like count.

Testcase Name: Like a post with a non-existent share ID
Testcase Objective: Verify system rejects a like request for a share ID that does not exist.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call POST /api/v2/buzz/shares/99999999/likes | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns an invalid-parameter error and no like is recorded.

Testcase Name: Like a comment for the first time
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can like a comment that they have not previously liked.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Open a post with a comment | 3. Click Like on the comment | 4. Observe result
Expected Result: Like is registered and the comment's like count increases by 1.

Testcase Name: Attempt to like a comment that is already liked
Testcase Objective: Verify system prevents a user from liking the same comment twice.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who has already liked a comment | 2. Call POST /api/v2/buzz/comments/{commentId}/likes again | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 400 Bad Request with message Already liked and the like count remains unchanged.

Testcase Objective: Verify a user can remove their like from a comment they previously liked.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who has liked a comment | 2. Click Unlike on the comment | 3. Observe result
Expected Result: Like is removed and the comment's like count decreases by 1.

Testcase Name: Attempt to unlike a comment that was never liked
Testcase Objective: Verify system rejects an unlike request for a comment the user has not liked.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user who has not liked a specific comment | 2. Call DELETE /api/v2/buzz/comments/{commentId}/likes | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 400 Bad Request with message Not previously liked.

Testcase Name: List all likes on a comment sorted by liked date
Testcase Objective: Verify likes on a comment can be listed and sorted by likedAtUtc.
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/comments/{commentId}/likes?sortField=commentLike.likedAtUtc&sortOrder=DESC | 2. Inspect response order
Expected Result: Likes are returned ordered by most recently liked first, with the correct total count.

Testcase Name: Share an existing post without additional text
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can re-share an existing post to the feed without adding extra text.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Open a post in the feed | 3. Click Share | 4. Leave caption text empty | 5. Submit share
Expected Result: A new share entry (type=share) referencing the original post is created and appears in the feed under the sharing employee.

Testcase Name: Share an existing post with additional caption text
Testcase Objective: Verify a user can re-share an existing post along with their own caption text.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Open a post in the feed | 3. Click Share | 4. Enter caption text | 5. Submit share
Expected Result: A new share entry is created with the caption text displayed alongside the original shared post content.

Testcase Name: Share a post using a non-existent shareId
Testcase Objective: Verify system rejects a share request referencing a shareId that does not exist.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call POST /api/v2/buzz/shares with shareId=99999999 | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns an invalid-parameter error and no share is created.

Testcase Name: Share a post with caption text exceeding max length
Testcase Objective: Verify system rejects share caption text exceeding the 65530 character limit.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Attempt to share a post with caption text of 65531 characters | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: Validation error is returned and the share is not created.

Testcase Name: List all shares/reposts of a given post
Testcase Objective: Verify all shares of a specific post can be retrieved via the post shares listing endpoint.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/posts/{id}/shares | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: Response returns all share records (type=share) referencing that post, with the correct total count.

Testcase Name: Multiple employees independently share the same post
Testcase Objective: Verify multiple different employees can each independently share the same original post.
Steps: 1. Login as Employee A and share Post X | 2. Login as Employee B and share the same Post X | 3. Verify the feed
Expected Result: Two separate share entries are created, both referencing the same original post, and each appears under its respective sharer's name in the feed.

Testcase Objective: Verify a user can edit the caption text of their own re-shared post.
Steps: 1. Login as employee who shared a post with caption text | 2. Click Edit on own share | 3. Update caption text | 4. Save changes
Expected Result: Share caption text is updated successfully.

Testcase Name: Attempt to edit an original post via the shares edit endpoint
Testcase Objective: Verify system blocks editing an original post (type=post) through the /buzz/shares/{id} update endpoint.
Steps: 1. Login as post owner | 2. Call PUT /api/v2/buzz/shares/{id} where id refers to the original post's share record (type=post) | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns an invalid-parameter error, since original posts must be edited via /buzz/posts/{id}, not /buzz/shares/{id}.

Testcase Name: Attempt to edit another employee's share
Testcase Objective: Verify a regular ESS user cannot edit a re-share authored by another employee.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user A | 2. Call PUT /api/v2/buzz/shares/{id} for a share authored by employee B | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 403 Forbidden and the share remains unchanged.

Testcase Name: Delete own re-share without affecting the original post
Testcase Objective: Verify deleting a re-share (type=share) removes only that share entry and leaves the original post intact.
Steps: 1. Login as employee who re-shared a post | 2. Click Delete/Unshare on own share entry | 3. Confirm deletion | 4. Verify original post still exists in feed
Expected Result: Only the share record is deleted; the original post and other shares of it remain visible in the feed.

Testcase Name: Delete original post via the shares delete endpoint
Testcase Objective: Verify deleting a share record of type post removes the entire original post, cascading photos, comments, likes, and shares.
Steps: 1. Login as post owner | 2. Call DELETE /api/v2/buzz/shares/{id} where id is the original post's share record | 3. Confirm deletion
Expected Result: The original post and its associated content are permanently deleted, and any re-shares of it are also removed from the feed.

Testcase Name: Attempt to delete another employee's re-share
Testcase Objective: Verify a regular ESS user cannot delete or unshare a re-share entry created by another employee.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user A | 2. Call DELETE /api/v2/buzz/shares/{id} for a share authored by employee B | 3. Submit request
Expected Result: API returns 403 Forbidden and the share is not deleted.

Testcase Name: View upcoming work anniversaries within next 30 days
Testcase Objective: Verify employees whose joining-date anniversary falls within the next 0 to 30 days are listed.
Steps: 1. Login as ESS user | 2. Navigate to Buzz module | 3. View the Upcoming Anniversaries widget/feed
Expected Result: All employees whose work anniversary date (based on joinedDate) falls between today and 30 days from now are listed.

Testcase Name: Anniversary falling exactly today is included (0-day boundary)
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee whose anniversary date is exactly today (date difference equals 0) is included in the list.
Steps: 1. Set up an employee whose joinedDate month and day match today's date in a prior year | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/anniversaries | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: The employee is included in the anniversary list.

Testcase Name: Anniversary exactly 30 days away is included (upper boundary)
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee whose anniversary date is exactly 30 days from today is included in the results.
Steps: 1. Set up an employee whose anniversary date is exactly 30 days from today | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/anniversaries | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: The employee is included in the anniversary list since the date difference equals the max boundary of 30.

Testcase Objective: Verify an employee whose anniversary date is 31 days from today is excluded from the upcoming anniversaries list.
Steps: 1. Set up an employee whose anniversary date is 31 days from today | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/anniversaries | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: The employee is not included in the results, since 31 exceeds the maximum of 30 days.

Testcase Name: Employee who joined in the current year is excluded
Testcase Objective: Verify an employee whose joinedDate year equals the current year is excluded from the anniversary list since they have not completed a full year.
Steps: 1. Set up an employee who joined earlier this calendar year | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/anniversaries | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: The newly joined employee does not appear in the upcoming anniversaries list.

Testcase Name: Terminated or purged employees are excluded from anniversary list
Testcase Objective: Verify employees with a termination record or purged status are excluded from the upcoming anniversaries feed even if their anniversary date falls within range.
Steps: 1. Set up a terminated employee and a purged employee both with anniversary dates within the next 30 days | 2. Call GET /api/v2/buzz/anniversaries | 3. Inspect response
Expected Result: Neither the terminated nor the purged employee appears in the results.
